{"subject":"GC pauses and p99 on Cassandra leaderboards","body":"Hi Lior,

Thanks for connecting. Your talk on running 60 self-managed Apache Cassandra nodes for the Kestrel Games leaderboard stuck with me, especially the tail latency and GC/compaction tuning side of it.

That tuning burden is exactly what ScyllaDB's design targets: a shard-per-core C++ architecture with no JVM garbage-collection pauses, so p99 stays predictable without the constant GC work.

If it's useful, I'd be glad to share how that maps to a leaderboard-style workload. Open to a short exchange on it?

Oz
GTM Engineer, ScyllaDB

Reply STOP to opt out.","evidence_ids":["s06"],"value_prop_ids":["vp_latency"],"context_fact_ids":[]}
